entities.summary: Sir Thomas Playford was an Australian politician from the state of South Australia. He served as Premier of South Australia and leader of the Liberal and Country League (LCL) from 5 November 1938 to 10 March 1965. Though controversial, it was the longest term of any elected government leader in Australian history. His tenure as premier was marked by a period of population and economic growth unmatched by any other Australian state. He was known for his parochial style in pushing South Australia's interests, and was known for his ability to secure a disproportionate share of federal funding for the state as well as his shameless haranguing of federal leaders.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Premier of South Australia from 1938 to 1965, Thomas Playford's leadership marked a period of unprecedented population and economic growth, with his state becoming one of the most prosperous in Australia. His legacy has had lasting regional impact on Australian politics.
